clause_6_v2_verbatim.face_qualifier_mandatory_on_warrants: WARRANT-onset, WARRANT-close and WARRANT-rival carry a face qualifier: ':near' (the seam verse inside the unit the seam bounds — the row's first verse for its onset, its last verse for its close, the candidate onset verse for a rival), ':far' (the adjacent verse across the seam), ':interior' (an in-span verse the warrant rests on that is neither — e.g. the מופת partner at 24:24 for the 24:27 close; permitted for WARRANT-close and WARRANT-onset only when the annotation names the device). Form: 'oshb:Ezek.33.20 [WARRANT-onset:far] pe-marked close behind the dateline'. For WARRANT-onset and WARRANT-close the member DERIVES the face from (verse, span) and FAILS LOUD on a mismatch, so the qualifier is verified, not free text. For WARRANT-rival the seam is not in the schema, so the annotation's first token names the seam pair — 'oshb:Ezek.33.12 [WARRANT-rival:near] 33.11/33.12 ve'attah, same audience, unlicensed' — and the member checks the ref's verse is one side of the pair and the qualifier matches that side.
clause_6_v2_verbatim.absence_tokens: WARRANT-absence (a single verse or a range; the boundary rests on the absence — 'no formula, mark, K/Q or paseq at C:V' or 'inside C:V-C:V') and DISCLOSURE-absence (a single verse or a range; recorded, the boundary does not rest on it — the honest home for 'device census records no stroke here'). WARRANT-absence-over-range is retained as a deprecated alias the member accepts and maps to WARRANT-absence. The citation sweep's mark, paseq and puncta arms treat any *-absence token as a NEGATED claim and verify the census is EMPTY at the verse(s): a false absence (device present) is a defect (Q6.2).
clause_6_v2_verbatim.worked_example_per_token: the author brief carries one worked example per token, including the three cases lane 01 found divergent: a verse with neither device nor mark that the rationale rests on (WARRANT with :near/:far, the ground named — content is a warrant when the rationale rests on it); an inventoried device the boundary does not rest on (DISCLOSURE-device, never ANCHOR); a device that is not recorded (never DISCLOSURE-device; ANCHOR or *-absence).
clause_6_v2_verbatim.face_of_the_evidence: X2 (lane 02): an MT-borne device (mark, paseq, K/Q, note, formula membership) is cited on the oshb: face; a WEB quotation on the web: face; inside the ch 20/21 zone every entry is dual as already ruled. Outside the zone this is a deterministic re-face (identity numbering) and runs as a MECHANICAL sweep with a distinct check; the two rows lane 02 names as inverting near/far in prose (P11-001, P11-013) are in the prose pass.
clause_6_v2_verbatim.retro_qualification: The 'existing entries are NOT re-tokenised' clause is amended for ONE deterministic case: every WARRANT-onset and WARRANT-close token this wave installed receives its derived face qualifier by a mechanical sweep (derivable from verse and span; adds information; changes no claim), distinct-checked. WARRANT-rival tokens receive the qualifier and seam pair in the author repair batch (author work: the seam must be read off the SRA). Pre-wave descriptive entries are still not re-tokenised.
clause_6_v2_verbatim.why_a_qualifier_and_not_a_split_token: a split (WARRANT-onset-near / WARRANT-onset-far) doubles the vocabulary and still leaves the rival unsaid; a qualifier the member verifies is smaller and auditable.

A pe is recorded after this verse; the inventory does not carry intra-verse position, so no claim is made about whether the mark falls before or after 3:17's watchman charge, צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.3.17) (“I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.3.17)). Close: 3:21, at the second samekh, before the hand-of-YHWH reopens the scene at 3:22.
live.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit backward to include 3:12-3:15, uniting the return-journey and the watchman charge under one 'onset at 3:12' reading. live.boundary_rationale: Onset: 4:1 וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ קַח לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.4.1) (“You also, son of man, take a tile” (web:Ezek.4.1)), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset that opens P2 (one of the book's 23 occurrences of that construction), immediately after the parent seam weighed at oshb:Ezek.3.27 above. The same siege-tile complex continues through the lying sign-acts at 4:4 and the food-rationing at 4:9 without a matching 'son of man' sub-onset at either point (both open with the bare 've'attah' alone), so all three stages read as one commanded symbolic act rather than three. At 4:8, וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.4.8) (“Behold, I put ropes on you” (web:Ezek.4.8)) recurs the exact word from 3:25 on the far side of the parent seam, disclosed as continuity evidence the seam-assessment above already weighed. A second address at 4:16, בֶּן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.16), intensifies rather than restarts the act (“behold, I will break the staff of bread” (web:Ezek.4.16)). Close: 4:17, לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ezek.4.17) (“that they may lack bread and water” (web:Ezek.4.17)), with a pe recorded after it, before 5:1 opens a distinct sign-act with its own 'son of man' address.
live.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the tile sign-act (4:1-4:3) from the lying and food-rationing sign-acts (4:4-4:17) as two units. This is the question the division plan holds for chs 4-7, and the 4:3/4:4 seam is its strongest form. Named and weighed under A9: on the near face the witness records a samekh after oshb:Ezek.4.3, and that verse closes on the sign-act colophon א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.4.3), “This shall be a sign to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.4.3), standing verse-final. On the far face oshb:Ezek.4.4 carries no formula whatever: in the pinned inventory no verse of ch 4 belongs to the messenger, utterance, recognition or word-event classes, the chapter's only listed members being the son-of-man address at 4:1 and 4:16 and the year-word non-datelines at 4:5-4:6. The colophon is not a close-role formula - oshb:Ezek.4.3 is absent from both the 81-verse utterance list and the 64-verse recognition family - so CUT-RULE's second limb is not met; and the addressee is unchanged across the seam, 2ms imperatives standing to the prophet on either side, so its first limb is not met either. A mark alone never satisfies limb (b). The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, held on those grounds, and the samekh is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates rather than for this row. The test is reworded because its earlier form omitted 4:3, the very verse the mark follows: the titled sub-onset וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ stands at 4:1 and again at 5:1, whereas bare וְאַתָּ֤ה without the title opens three interior stages - 4:3, 4:4 and 4:9 - so the text stages the siege-model, the iron pan, the two lying postures and the rationed food as one commanded act and not as separate commands (oshb:Ezek.4.1).
live.device_notes: 17-verse unit, one verse past the 14-16 stretch cap for measured or listed blocks; disclosed rather than forced into an unsupported cut, since no formula-marked seam stands between 4:3/4:4 or 4:8/4:9. Two K/Q verses checked before quoting (4:6, 4:15); 4:6 also carries an editorial note tied to the same disputed consonant, disclosed together. Paseq at 4:9 disclosed count-only, single-witness. MT 3:27 is followed by a samekh (single witness); the sign-act series that opens at 4:1 has this mark standing immediately before it. Inside the span a samekh follows MT 4:12 (single witness); the unit does not cut there because the food-rationing act begun at 4:9 continues without a fresh 'son of man' address or messenger formula reopening the speech. A further samekh stands after MT 4:14 (single witness) inside the span; no cut is made there either, since 4:15's concession is Yahweh's reply within the same rationing scene, not a fresh address.

live.boundary_rationale: Onset: 5:1 וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן אָדָ֜ם קַח לְךָ֣ חֶ֣רֶב חַדָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.5.1) (“You, son of man, take a sharp sword” (web:Ezek.5.1)), a fresh 'son of man' sub-onset distinct from 4:1's - a new symbolic object (sword/razor/hair) rather than a continuation of the siege-tile act. The messenger formula at 5:5, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.5.5), opens the act's own interpretation rather than a competing unit (no refrain close intervenes between the hair-sign and its meaning). The oath at 5:11, חַי אָ֗נִי ('as I live'), with the utterance signature נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.5.11) attached mid-verse, marks an emphatic sub-onset of the verdict paragraph, not a unit boundary. The formula 'I, Yahweh, have spoken' recurs three times, at 5:13 (אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ (oshb:Ezek.5.13)), 5:15 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.15)) and 5:17 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.17)); the first two are paragraph-final rather than unit-final because no fresh onset device follows either (5:14 continues “Moreover I will make you a desolation” (web:Ezek.5.14) with no messenger formula or word-event reopening the address). Close: 5:17, with a pe recorded after it, before 6:1 opens with a fresh strict word-event. The verdict continues in two further 'therefore' messenger formulae addressing the same party: 5:7, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.7) (2mp, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says'), and 5:8, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.8) (2fs, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says') — both verdict paragraphs inside the same interpretation, addressing Jerusalem and the people in her as one party, with no refrain standing before either (the samekh after 5:6, 5:7 and 5:9 are disclosed as intra-row texture, not unit-cutting seams). The verdict is bound to the sign-act itself by a byte-identical clause: 5:12 closes with the same words that close 5:2, וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.5.2; oshb:Ezek.5.12) ('and I will draw a sword after them', sweep: 3 verses book-wide, the third at 12:14).
live.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 5:13 or 5:15, the first two 'I Yahweh have spoken' occurrences, to shorten the unit. Rejected because neither is followed by a fresh onset device - the material after each continues the same verdict speech without a messenger formula, word-event or address restarting it - so only 5:17's occurrence is unit-final. The stronger rival, weighed here under A16, is the 5:4/5:5 seam, the division the division plan holds for this chapter (the sign-act 5:1-4 set against the interpretation 5:5-17). Its near face carries a PE recorded after oshb:Ezek.5.4 and nothing further: that verse ends מִמֶּ֥נּוּ תֵצֵא אֵ֖שׁ אֶל כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and it appears in neither the utterance inventory nor the 64-member recognition family, so it does not close on a close-role formula. Its far face is genuinely strong, oshb:Ezek.5.5 carrying the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה verse-initially, “The Lord Yahweh says” (web:Ezek.5.5). But CUT-RULE makes a messenger formula a sub-onset only where the addressee changes or the preceding verse has closed on a verse-final close-role formula, and neither limb holds at this seam: 5:4 addresses the prophet in the 2ms while 5:5 carries no second person at all, the shift to 2mp arriving only at 5:7 and to 2fs at 5:8; and a parashah mark cannot meet that limb by itself. The row accordingly holds the seam on those stated grounds, and the PE is recorded as corroboration of the rival and not of this unit's onset.
live.device_notes: 17-verse unit, one verse past the 14-16 stretch cap; disclosed rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut, as at oshb:Ezek.4.1-4.17, since no refrain-plus-fresh-onset pair stands anywhere inside 5:1-5:17 to license a shorter cut. Paseq at 5:1 and 5:7 disclosed count-only, single-witness. Marks after 5:4 (pe), 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 (samekh) and 5:10 (pe) are disclosed as intra-row, single-witness texture. An earlier ground stated here was false and is corrected: three of those five marks DO coincide with a formula onset on the verse following them. The pe after 5:4 stands before the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.5.5, and the samekh marks after 5:6 and 5:7 stand before the messenger formulae at oshb:Ezek.5.7 and oshb:Ezek.5.8; each of those three verses is a member of the inventory's 122-verse messenger class and each carries the formula verse-initially, 5:7 behind לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Ezek.5.7) and 5:8 behind לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Ezek.5.8). The remaining two do not: oshb:Ezek.5.10 opens on לָכֵ֗ן with no messenger formula, and oshb:Ezek.5.11 opens on the oath with the utterance signature attached mid-verse. No one of the five is read as a unit-cutting seam, but the reason is CUT-RULE and not any absence of coincidence: not one of them follows a verse that ENDS on a close-role formula, since none of 5:4, 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 or 5:10 appears in either the utterance inventory or the 64-member recognition family, and a parashah mark by itself cannot license the cut. Single witness: a pe stands after MT 4:17, the mark on record at the seam where this unit begins.

The row is extended through a second transport at oshb:Ezek.8.16 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל חֲצַ֣ר בֵּית יְהוָה֮ הַפְּנִימִית֒ וְהִנֵּה פֶ֜תַח הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה בֵּ֤ין הָֽאוּלָם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ אֲחֹ֨רֵיהֶ֜ם אֶל הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וּפְנֵיהֶ֣ם קֵ֔דְמָה וְהֵ֛מָּה מִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֥ם קֵ֖דְמָה לַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (the sun-worshippers, “about twenty-five men… their backs toward Yahweh's temple” (web:Ezek.8.16)) because the bar on a row under three verses that is not a complete word-event unit bars the shorter row a cut before 8:16 would leave — that ground is stated and weighed in the rejected alternative, and no mark-absence is offered for or against any seam here. Close: oshb:Ezek.8.18 וְגַם אֲנִי֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה בְחֵמָ֔ה לֹֽא תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמֹ֑ל וְקָרְא֤וּ בְאָזְנַי֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁמַ֖ע אוֹתָֽם is the wrath declaration — “I will also deal in wrath… I will not hear them” (web:Ezek.8.18) — a narrative and thematic close (the fourfold tableau's climax) rather than a recognition or utterance refrain; oshb:Ezek.9.1 opens the next scene with the loud-voiced cry that sets the executioners in motion, which is the strongest available onset-side confirmation that 8:18 is where the temple-tour proper ends.

Its near face is the pointer close at oshb:Ezek.8.15, the third of this tour's forward-pointing 'you will again see' transitions (8:6, 8:13, 8:15); its far face is oshb:Ezek.8.16, a transport verse that is a member of the division plan's closed transport list and a scene seam the division plan names by verse (8:5, 8:7, 8:14, 8:16). The rival is therefore licensed on both faces and it is not dismissed. The row holds because the bar on a row under three verses that is not a complete word-event unit governs what a licensed driver may yield: a cut before 8:16 leaves 8:14-8:15, and MEASURED against the verse census, whose declared face is WEB, that is only 2 verses while the remainder 8:16-8:18 has 3 — the guard allows a row under three verses only when it is a complete word-event unit, and 8:14-8:15 is not one. The samekh recorded on MT 8:14 is entered as support for the alternative it favours and no wider: this inventory keys a mark to the verse it stands after, so honouring it as a close would stop the row at 8:14 by itself, which the guard bars outright, and a section break carries corroborating weight only, ranking below every licensed driver.
